title: Interceptors: CallHandler, next.handle(), and RxJS Response Pipelines

progressiveExplaining.eli5: An interceptor is like a wrapper around a gift box. Before the present is made, the interceptor can check the stopwatch (`tap`). After the present is built, the interceptor wraps it in shiny paper and adds a greeting card (`map`) or catches it if it drops and breaks (`catchError`).
progressiveExplaining.junior: Interceptors implement the `NestInterceptor` interface with `intercept(context, next: CallHandler): Observable<any>`. They use Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP) to bind extra logic before and after method execution. By calling `next.handle()`, you invoke the route handler and receive an RxJS `Observable` of the response, which you can transform using operators like `map()` (wrap response in `{ data: ... }`), `tap()` (log execution time), or `timeout()`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Interceptors wrap the execution pipeline using the RxJS stream contract. Unlike Guards (which only control binary entry), Interceptors have dual access: synchronous pre-execution logic runs before `next.handle()`, while asynchronous post-execution logic runs in the returned Observable pipeline. This makes them ideal for response envelope serialization, cache management, distributed tracing span injection, and request timing metrics.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: `CallHandler.handle()` returns an Observable stream originating from the controller method. NestJS's internal `InterceptorsConsumer` nests all bound interceptors into a single chained Observable composition: `interceptor1(context, { handle: () => interceptor2(context, next) })`. The final resolved stream is subscribed to by the HTTP adapter, which serializes the emitted value to the client socket.

codeComparison.title: Manual Controller Response Wrapping vs Global Transform Interceptor
codeComparison.summary: Manually wrapping responses in `{ data: ... }` pollutes controller logic; an Interceptor normalizes all API responses cleanly.

legacyOrBad.label: Manual Controller Envelope Wrapping
legacyOrBad.snippet: return { data: users, timestamp: Date.now() }; // ❌ Duplicated across every controller

modernOrGood.label: RxJS Transform Interceptor
modernOrGood.snippet: return next.handle().pipe(map(data => ({ data, timestamp: new Date().toISOString() }))); // ✅ NEW

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if you do NOT call `next.handle()` inside an Interceptor?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of interceptor pipeline propagation.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: If you do not call `next.handle()`, the **route handler method will never be executed**. You can use this behavior deliberately to short-circuit requests (e.g. returning cached responses directly from memory via `of(cachedData)` without hitting the controller or database).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Returning a plain value without calling `next.handle()` or returning an `Observable` will hang the HTTP connection.

interviewGotchas.question: How can an Interceptor handle request timeouts in NestJS?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of RxJS operator integration with NestJS interceptors.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Ensure `RequestTimeoutException` from `@nestjs/common` is thrown so NestJS serializes an HTTP 408 response.
